proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, and let t be a real number with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n. Since k>0, multiplying the inequality (n-1)/n <= t by k preserves the order, giving k(n-1)/n <= kt. Also, because k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, hence
k(n-1)/n = k - k/n >= k - 1.
Therefore kt >= k-1. On the other hand, t < 1 implies kt < k. So
k-1 <= kt < k.
Because k-1 and k are consecutive integers, this means floor(kt) = k-1. Since k was arbitrary, the conclusion holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.
solver_summary: For t in [(n-1)/n,1), one has k-1 <= kt < k for every 1<=k<=n, so floor(kt)=k-1.
